(This references ISO 27005 risk-management *guidelines* only; no ISO 27001 certification is claimed anywhere on the trust center or security page.)

certifications.name: HIPAA
certifications.proof_quote: Trust center 'Data collected' lists 'Personal health information' as a data category, but no HIPAA compliance, BAA, or attestation is claimed. Treat as not offered absent confirmation.

privacy.terms_url: https://www.builder.io/legal (SaaS Services Agreement / SaaS Terms); AI Terms also published at https://www.builder.io/legal
privacy.ai_training_note: Plan-dependent and this is the most important nuance for buyers. Verbatim from the AI-use doc: Free plans -> 'Builder may use customer data to train and improve the AI.' Self-serve paid plans -> 'Customer data may be used to train the AI only if AI content training is toggled On' (opt-in, default behavior should be confirmed in-product). Enterprise plans -> 'Builder does not use customer data from Enterprise accounts for AI training or improvement purposes.' Third-party LLMs -> 'Builder currently uses OpenAI and Anthropic's Claude. We may also use open-source LLMs, such as Mistral or Llama 2' and 'The third-party LLMs we use do not train on your data.' Proprietary models -> 'Builder's proprietary AI models are fully built and trained internally and hosted on Google Cloud.' Marketing/blog claim: 'We don't train on your data.' trains_on_customer_data is recorded as false for paid/enterprise (the directory's relevant audience), but note the free-tier exception.
privacy.data_region: United States and other countries (global). Privacy policy: 'Your information may be stored and processed in - and we may transfer information to - the U.S. and other countries.' No EU-only/region-pinned residency offered publicly. Standard cross-border transfer language for EU users.

security.name: Penetration testing
security.value: Performed (listed as a Product security control on the trust center). Security page also describes manual source-code analysis, peer review, static analysis, threat modeling, and OWASP-based design/testing.

security.name: Bug bounty / VDP
security.value: None found. No HackerOne or Bugcrowd program and no published vulnerability disclosure program located on the vendor domain or via search. Security contact is support@builder.io.

security.name: Encryption
security.value: TLS in transit ('all communications ... are encrypted using ... Transport Layer Security (TLS)'); data encryption at rest ('Data encryption utilized' control); passwords hashed with a random salt; encryption key access restricted.

security.name: Access controls
security.value: SSO, strong passwords and/or 2FA required for employee access to production; least-privilege internal access; account lockout on repeated failed logins; per-session unique identifiers.

security.name: Resilience / availability
security.value: Daily/weekly/monthly backups tested regularly; multi-data-center replication; documented and tested Incident Response Plan; Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery plans established and tested; cybersecurity insurance maintained.

security.name: Subprocessors (disclosed)
security.value: Google Cloud Platform (primary production hosting + holds internal model hosting), Amazon Web Services (CDN + logging), Fastly (CDN), Anthropic (LLM hosting). Full list available on the trust center.

security.name: Hosting
security.value: Google Cloud Platform and Amazon Web Services. Biometric-controlled data centers; vendor relies on cloud providers' physical-security attestations.

products.name: Visual Copilot (Figma plugin / design-to-code)
products.data_scope: Sends design/Figma content and prompts to third-party LLMs (OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, possibly Mistral/Llama) and to Builder's GCP-hosted internal models. 600,000+ plugin users cited. Third-party LLMs do not train on the data; 'Match My Code Style' / Component Mapping use customer code components.
products.notes: GA since March 2024; Visual Copilot 2.0 ('Design to Interactive') announced later. Now folded into Builder's broader platform (Fusion).

products.name: Builder.io Free / self-serve plans
products.data_scope: Free tier: customer data MAY be used to train/improve AI. Self-serve paid: AI training only if the customer toggles 'AI content training' On.
products.notes: This is the key compliance differentiator vs Enterprise. Procurement-sensitive teams should be on a paid plan with training off, or Enterprise.

products.name: Builder.io Enterprise
products.data_scope: No customer data used for AI training or improvement. SOC 2 Type II report available under request/NDA. Enterprise SLA and Enterprise Support Terms published.
products.notes: Best fit for regulated/security-conscious buyers. Trust center access and SOC 2 report are request-gated (Vanta).

compare.pricing_model: Freemium SaaS: free tier, self-serve paid tiers, and Enterprise (custom). Per the pricing page and 'Pricing' nav.
compare.data_residency: US/global; no public region-pinned residency option. Cross-border transfer language for EU users.

flags: AI-training behavior is plan-dependent: FREE tier may use customer data to train AI; self-serve paid is opt-in; only Enterprise is contractually no-training. The blanket marketing claim 'We don't train on your data' is accurate only for third-party LLMs and for paid/enterprise, not for the free tier.
No public bug bounty or VDP program found.
No ISO 27001 certification (only ISO 27005 risk-methodology reference). Do not list ISO 27001.
Trust center 'Data collected' lists 'Personal health information' and 'Credit card information' as categories, but no HIPAA/PCI attestation is claimed; HIPAA marked unknown/not offered.
SOC 2 report and full trust center are request-gated (Vanta) rather than openly downloadable.
DPA not directly located in public evidence; GDPR/CCPA posture and subprocessor list are public, but a signed DPA likely sits behind sales/enterprise.
